SECTION 3: STUDY NOTES (READ AND LEARN)

WHAT YOU ARE STUDYING: ANIMALS ENVIRONMENT
Subject: ENVIRONMENTAL ACTIVITIES · Grade: PP2
This is a learner study lesson (not a teacher guide). Read every part, follow the models, then practise.

BIG PICTURE
Animals ENVIRONMENT helps you succeed in ENVIRONMENTAL ACTIVITIES. You will understand it, practise it, and use it in your school compound, home, farm, or county.

KEY FACTS ABOUT ANIMALS
Animals are living things. They move, feed, grow, and respond to their surroundings.
Domestic animals live with people (cow, goat, chicken, dog, cat).
Wild animals live on their own in forests, parks, or water (lion, zebra, fish).
In Kenya you may see cows in a homestead, fish at a market, or birds on the school field.
Safety: do not touch unknown animals; wash hands after handling pets or farm animals.

PART 1: Observe animals • Learners to be taken for a nature walk within the to observe animals environment, • Learners could feed the domestic

What this means
In this part you learn to observe animals • Learners to be taken for a nature walk within the to observe animals environment, • Learners could feed the domestic. You will use ideas from in your school compound, home, farm, or county.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: observe animals • Learners to be taken for a nature walk within the to observe animals environment, • Learners could feed the domestic.
2. Observe, explain, then apply using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Observe: Name what you can see/touch about “Animals ENVIRONMENT” around your school.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can observe animals • Learners to be taken for a nature walk within the to observe animals environment, • Learners could feed the domestic. Write or say your answer clearly.

PUT IT TOGETHER
Close your notes and say aloud: what Animals ENVIRONMENT is, one example, and one way you will practise this week.

SECTION 4: QUICK EXAMPLES

Domestic animals live with people (cow, goat, chicken, dog, cat).

Wild animals live on their own in forests, parks, or water (lion, zebra, fish).

Example 1: Name what you can see/touch about “Animals ENVIRONMENT” around your school. (skill: observe animals • Learners to be taken for a nature walk within the to observe animals environment, • Learners could feed the domestic)

SECTION 5: PRACTICE NOW

1. Write 5 sentences (or show 5 clear steps) that teach Animals ENVIRONMENT to a classmate.
2. Practise this skill: observe animals • Learners to be taken for a nature walk within the to observe animals environment, • Learners could feed the domestic.
3. Make one local Kenya example of Animals ENVIRONMENT from your county, market, farm, or school.
4. Mark your own work: What did you get right? What will you redo?

SECTION 6: WORK TO DO (HOME / REVISION)

1. In your exercise book, make a one-page revision sheet for Animals ENVIRONMENT: meaning, 3 examples, 5 practice items.
2. Teach a parent/guardian or younger sibling one part of this lesson (2 minutes).
3. Answer in writing: Why should a PP2 learner study Animals ENVIRONMENT?
4. Prepare for the quiz: cover the Remember box and recite it.

SECTION: REMEMBER

1. Know what Animals ENVIRONMENT means in your own words.
2. Use local Kenyan examples, not only definitions.
3. Practise in small steps, then check your work.
4. Be able to: observe animals • Learners to be taken for a nature walk within the to observe animals environment, • Learners could feed the domestic.

Now complete the Revision Quiz. Open Answers only after you finish.
